Tidy per-actor endpoint summary of a wide-format sequence dataset

Source: R/sequence_terminal.R
actor_endpoints.Rd

actor_endpoints() returns one row per sequence (actor) of a wide-format sequence table, with its first and last observed states, the positions where they occur, the number of observed cells and whether the sequence ends early. A sequence ends early (dropped_out) when its last observed state comes before the last column, so every cell after it is missing: the terminal-NA pattern of drop-out, course end or censoring. Internal gaps do not count.

The flag records only where the observations stop; it cannot say why. A sequence recorded over fewer positions than the others looks the same as one that left. mark_terminal_state() turns the terminal-NA cells into an explicit end state, and chain_structure() then describes the chain with that state.

Usage

actor_endpoints(data, cols = NULL)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a matrix or data frame with one row per actor and one column per position, holding state labels, with NA for a missing observation. Without cols, every column is read as a position, so the frame must be one column or a numbered run of positions (T1, T2, ...); a frame with other columns beside them, such as an id, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. A table from mark_terminal_state() or mark_first_state() is read as it is, because those functions mark their columns as positions.

cols

The columns holding the positions, in order; the other columns are ignored. A name not in data raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Default NULL (every column).

Value

A data frame with one row per actor and the columns:

actor

The row name when data has row names other than 1, 2, ...; otherwise the row number.

first_state, last_state

The first and the last observed state.

first_step, last_step

The positions (column numbers among the position columns) of the first and the last observed state.

n_observed

The number of observed cells.

dropped_out

TRUE when last_step is before the last column, so the row ends in missing cells.

A row with no observed state has NA states and steps, n_observed 0 and dropped_out FALSE.

See also

mark_terminal_state(), chain_structure()

Examples

actor_endpoints(trajectories) |> head()
#>   actor first_state last_state first_step last_step n_observed dropped_out
#> 1     1      Active     Active          1        12         12        TRUE
#> 2     2     Average    Average          1        15         15       FALSE
#> 3     3     Average     Active          1        15         15       FALSE
#> 4     4      Active    Average          1        15         15       FALSE
#> 5     5      Active    Average          1        15         15       FALSE
#> 6     6     Average    Average          1        15         15       FALSE
